text:
Mathieu Joseph scored shorthanded in Carolina on Nov 21, his fourth goal of the season, in a game the Oilers lost 7-4. NHL.com ran a piece days earlier on the mojo he found winning two Stanley Cups with Tampa Bay. Now he's on his fifth NHL team, in Edmonton, doing depth work.

The goals are running ahead of the chances: four on 2.2 expected, shooting 19% against a typical 13.5%. That won't last at this rate. The bigger issue is at five on five, where Edmonton gets only 34% of the expected goals with him on, 15 points worse than without him. He's been a penalty killer and a hitter (58 hits), and the line he plays on isn't asked to drive play, but those are tough numbers.

Evolving-Hockey had a gentler picture last season: he took chances away at the 86th percentile, and drew more penalties than he took. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 75% of his shots coming off the rush.

What to watch: whether the defensive side of his game shows up in the numbers. His minutes have dropped to 11 a night recently.
